label: Today you will learn
h: How to tell when useful thinking has become mental circling.
body: About 8 minutes, plus one short pause · one small practice · no homework list

label: Key Scripture
h: “When the cares of my heart are many, your consolations cheer my soul.”

label: Meet Grace
h:
Her body was in bed.
Her mind was still in meetings.

label: Mental circling is different
h: It returns to the same question and produces nothing new.
body: <svg viewBox="0 0 400 400" class=loop aria-label="A looping arrow returning to its start"><path d="M 200 60 A 140 140 0 1 1 90 120" fill="none" stroke="#c78a2c" stroke-width="18" stroke-linecap="round"/><polygon points="70,90 120,110 85,150" fill="#c78a2c"/><text x="200" y="215" text-anchor="middle" font-size="34" fill="currentColor">Same question</text><text x="200" y="260" text-anchor="middle" font-size="34" fill="currentColor">Same worry</text></svg>

label: Ask one question
h: Where is this thought taking me?
body: If the honest answer is “back to where I started,” you are circling.

label: Thinking or circling?
body:
Useful thinking

  • Gathers facts
  • Moves towards action
  • Has a stopping point

Mental circling

  • Repeats fears
  • Returns to the beginning
  • Often seeks complete certainty

label: What may be underneath it
h: “I am trying to feel completely certain before I allow myself to rest.”

label: Do this now
h: Name one matter your mind keeps returning to.
body:
Write it in one sentence. Do not solve it. Just name it.

Pause the audio

label: Remember
h: A crowded mind is not proof of weak faith.

label: Prayer
body:
Father, you already know
what my mind keeps returning to.

I bring it to you as it is — unsolved.

When the cares of my heart are many,
let your comfort cheer my soul.

Amen.
